text:
This looks like mid-2018. Fed funds near 1.91% fits May or June 2018, since the June 2018 hike took the rate to about 1.91% effective. Unemployment of 3.8% matches May 2018, and the 10-year yield at 2.84% fits May or June.

Headline CPI at 2.72% fits May 2018 (2.8%) better than June (2.9%). Core CPI at 2.21% fits April or May, so core CPI in May was about 2.2%.

The emerging-market equity 1-month return of -4.5% matches May 2018 or June 2018. The 3-month change in the dollar is large, which fits the April–May 2018 rally. The 2-year yield at 2.52% fits May 2018, when it was about 2.5%, and the 10-year at 2.84% fits May's end-of-month level of roughly 2.83%.

Gold at -3.6% over 1 month fits May 2018 (about -1.3%) or June 2018 (about -3.5%). That points to June, but the effective fed funds rate in May was 1.70% and in June was 1.82%. The monthly average for June 2018 was 1.91%, so June fits the rate. Unemployment in June was 4.0%, though, and May was 3.8%. The unemployment rate dropped 0.3 over 3 months, from 4.1% in March to 3.8% in May, which fits May. The monthly average fed funds rate in May 2018 was 1.70%, which does not match 1.91%. Mixed signals, but I lean toward June 2018 given the rate, the gold return, and EM equity being down. The 3-month payroll average of 179k also fits.
